source.publication: 2025 SC1040 Individual Income Tax Instructions (SCDOR) and the 2025 SC1040 form and tax tables (IITPacket_2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF pp.10-11 'Line p-1 through line p-3: Retirement deduction', qualified retirement income definition and Worksheet for taxpayer (line p-1) lines 1-5; Instructions PDF p.12 'Line q: Age 65 and older deduction' and Worksheet for taxpayer (line q-1) lines 1-4; PDF p.13 Examples 1-5 (Example 2); SC1040 lines 1-6 and 15 (packet PDF pp.46-47); Instructions PDF p.5 Line 1 (federal taxable income); Instructions PDF p.16 Line 6; Tax Rate Schedule packet PDF p.51 (6% minus 642, any filing status); brackets as derived in the record (brackets.derivation)

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 26,000.00 + IRA distribution 14,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 single + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 22,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, federal figures given, not tested). SC1040 line 1 federal taxable income 22,250.00; additions lines a-e none, line 2 = 0.00; line 3 = 22,250.00. Line p-1 worksheet (age 70): line 1 maximum 10,000.00; line 2 military 0.00; line 3 = 10,000.00; line 4 qualified retirement income = 26,000.00 + 14,000.00 = 40,000.00; line 5 lesser = 10,000.00 (cap binds). Line q-1 worksheet: 15,000.00 - (10,000.00 + 0.00) = 5,000.00 (as Example 2: 10,000 on p-1 and 5,000 on q-1; at the 15,000 combined maximum). Projection: best_of_group of the 65-or-older retirement entry (10,000) and the age 65 entry (min(15,000, 40,000) = 15,000) keeps 15,000; same total, so relief_amounts are not split by id. Line 4 total subtractions = p-1 10,000.00 + q-1 5,000.00 = 15,000.00. Line 5 South Carolina income subject to tax = 22,250.00 - 15,000.00 = 7,250.00. Line 6 tax = 3% x (7,250.00 - 3,560.00) = 3% x 3,690.00 = 110.70; the printed table (row 7,200 to 7,300, figured at the row midpoint) gives 111; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Line 12 Two Wage Earner Credit: not modelled (warning), 0.00; it is for joint filers only, so 0 anyway. Line 14 credits 0.00; line 15 state income tax = 110.70.
accepted_approximations: The bracket starts 3,560 and 17,840 are derived from the printed tax table and the 6%-minus-642 formula; the table fixes them only to 3,559-3,566 and 17,818-17,857. Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses the table row's midpoint.

The booklet stacks the age 65 deduction on the retirement deduction (15,000 less the retirement and military deductions taken). The projection puts the 65-or-older retirement deduction and the age 65 deduction in one best_of_group, with the age 65 cap reduced by military retirement. For a person 65 or older this gives the same total as the worksheets, the larger of 15,000 and the military retirement income (Examples 1-5), whenever the person's income covers it.
